days.title: Does the brain decide before you do?
days.summary: The timing holds; reading it as “no free will” does not.
days.survives: For arbitrary, purposeless movements, a slow brain signal begins several hundred ms before the reported urge. The reported urge is not the first measurable event — but nothing shows the brain decided unconsciously, and it doesn't cover real choices.

days.title: If one of three things must be true, are we simulated?
days.summary: The trilemma is valid logic, but it puts the odds of simulation near a third to a half, not “almost certainly”.
days.survives: You can't consistently believe all three: we'll reach posthuman tech, posthumans run many ancestor simulations, and we aren't simulated. But on its own the argument gives about 1/3 (Bostrom) to just under 1/2 (Kipping) odds of simulation, not near-certainty, and it says nothing about free will.

days.title: Can a brain scan see your choice 10 seconds early?
days.summary: The early signal is real, but it is a ~60% lean, not a prediction, and your past choices predict as well.
days.survives: In 12 pre-selected people, brain patterns guessed a left/right button press at about 55–60% (chance is 50%), starting about 7 s before they felt they decided. That is a small early lean, no better than guessing from their previous choices, and only the same lab has replicated it.
